formate.source: Cambridge English A2 Key, Information for candidates (ENG/97453/V1/MAY26) — https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/images/557749-a2-key-information-for-candidates.pdf, checked 2026-10-30
formate.intro: A2 Key has three papers: Reading and Writing, Listening and Speaking. Each paper is equally important, and you cannot fail a single paper: your overall score decides the result.

rows.what: Six short real-world texts (notices, signs, messages, emails): understand the main message
rows.time: 60 minutes for Reading and Writing together (one paper, Parts 1–7)

rows.what: Three short texts on the same topic: which text (A, B or C) says this?
rows.type: Multiple matching, A/B/C (texts can be used more than once)

rows.what: One longer text: detail, opinion and attitude
Multiple-choice cloze: one short text with gaps, mostly vocabulary
Open cloze: one or two short emails with gaps, mostly grammar words
rows.type: Write one word in each gap

rows.what: Guided writing: a short email or note covering three points
rows.time: same 60 minutes as Reading (Parts 6–7 of the paper)

rows.what: Picture story: write the story shown in three pictures
Five short recordings, one or two speakers: find the key information
rows.type: Multiple choice, 3 picture options (here: text options)
rows.time: about 30 minutes; on paper, 6 more minutes at the end to transfer answers

rows.what: One person speaking: complete notes
rows.type: Gap fill: 1 or 2 words, a number, a date or a time per gap

rows.what: One longer conversation: detail
Five short dialogues or monologues: main idea, message, place, purpose
One longer conversation: match five items to eight options
rows.type: Matching, options A–H (three are not used)

rows.what: Interview: basic factual and personal questions from the examiner
rows.type: Examiner and each candidate, about 3–4 minutes
rows.time: about 8–10 minutes, pairs (or groups of three), two examiners

rows.what: Collaborative discussion with picture prompts, then follow-up questions

formate.source: Cambridge English B1 Preliminary, exam format page and Handbook for teachers (2020 format) — https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/qualifications/preliminary/exam-format/; the live page could not be loaded on 2026-10-30, details from the handbook
formate.intro: B1 Preliminary has four papers: Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking. Your overall score on the Cambridge English Scale decides the result.

rows.what: Five short real-world texts: understand the main message
Five people's needs: match each person to one of eight short texts
rows.type: Matching, texts A–H (three are not used)

rows.what: One longer text: detail, opinion, attitude and the writer's purpose
Gapped text: five sentences have been taken out of a text
rows.type: Choose from eight sentences A–H (three are not used)

rows.what: Multiple-choice cloze: vocabulary in a short text
Open cloze: grammar words in a short text
rows.type: Write one word in each gap

rows.what: Email: answer an email using four notes
Article or story (choose one)
Seven short monologues or dialogues: key information
rows.type: Multiple choice, 3 picture options (here: text options)
rows.time: about 30 minutes including 6 minutes to transfer answers

rows.what: Six short dialogues: attitude and opinion
One monologue (e.g. a radio announcement): complete notes
rows.type: Gap fill, a word, number or short phrase per gap

rows.what: One longer interview: detail, attitude and opinion
Interview: personal questions
Long turn: describe a photograph
rows.type: Each candidate alone, about 1 minute each

rows.what: Collaborative task: discuss options from a situation with picture prompts
Discussion on the topic of Part 3

formate.source: Cambridge English B2 First, exam format page and Handbook for teachers — https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/qualifications/first/exam-format/; the live page could not be loaded on 2026-10-30, details from the handbook
formate.intro: B2 First has four papers: Reading and Use of English, Writing, Listening and Speaking. Your overall score on the Cambridge English Scale decides the result.

blocks.label: Paper 1: Reading and Use of English

rows.part: Reading and Use of English · Part 1
rows.what: Multiple-choice cloze: vocabulary (collocations, fixed phrases, phrasal verbs)

rows.part: Reading and Use of English · Part 2
rows.what: Open cloze: grammar words
rows.type: Write one word in each gap

rows.part: Reading and Use of English · Part 3
rows.what: Word formation: change the word in capitals to fit the gap

rows.part: Reading and Use of English · Part 4
rows.what: Key word transformation: same meaning with a given word, 2–5 words
rows.type: Write 2–5 words including the key word

rows.part: Reading and Use of English · Part 5
rows.what: One long text: detail, opinion, attitude, purpose, implication

rows.part: Reading and Use of English · Part 6
rows.what: Gapped text: six sentences have been taken out of a long text
rows.type: Choose from seven sentences A–G (one is not used)

rows.part: Reading and Use of English · Part 7
rows.what: Multiple matching: one text in sections or several short texts
rows.type: Matching, sections A–D/E (used more than once)

rows.what: Essay: give your opinion on a statement, using two given notes and one idea of your own
Choose one: article, email/letter, report or review
Eight short unrelated extracts: gist, detail, function, attitude
One monologue: complete sentences
rows.type: Sentence completion, a word or short phrase per gap

rows.what: Five short related monologues: match each speaker to an option
rows.type: Matching, options A–H (three are not used)

rows.what: One interview or discussion: opinion, attitude, detail
Interview: general and personal questions
Long turn: compare two photographs and answer a question, then comment on the partner's photos
rows.type: Each candidate about 1 minute, plus a 30-second response

rows.what: Collaborative task: discuss a question with five written prompts, then decide
Discussion on the topic of Part 3
